correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern head stream, small headward waterbodies and northeast elongate-lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning is a mountain stream running north through a small narrow waterbody, then northeast along a connected channel through an elongate lake and its eastern outlet. Original TRIM portrays the head setting, inlet, lake body, outlet and continuation, independently of selected model connectivity. The much larger lake to the north is not traversed.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact bank or vertex requirement.
correspondence.name_observation: The small headstream and both lake names remain null. The downstream McClinchy label is not extended automatically across these separate waterbodies.

correspondence.component_scope: McClinchy Creek upper tributary loop and receiving-river junction
correspondence.finding: Beyond the elongate lake, the selected tributary continues northeast, bends east/southeast at its northernmost reach, then south beside the road corridor. It reaches the river junction west of the broad lake on the receiving river. The selection takes the southwest/west receiving channel rather than traversing the broad lake to the east. Lateral lake chains and feeders are separately drawn.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact bank or vertex requirement.
correspondence.name_observation: The rescue map’s McClinchy Creek label belongs to this upper tributary corridor. Exact upstream/downstream legal naming boundaries and lake names are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Klinaklini receiving trunk, small waterbody passage and westward mountain bend
correspondence.finding: From the McClinchy-side junction the selected route follows the mapped receiving trunk west and southwest. It passes a small broadened waterbody before the substantial westward bend, receives a northern side branch and continues southwest/south. The retained original093C map covers this entire connector and overlaps both current TRIM sectors.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact bank or vertex requirement.
correspondence.name_observation: Klinaklini River is mapped on the receiving trunk. The intervening small waterbody and northern tributary names remain null. No scalar naming of a lake passage is implied.

correspondence.component_scope: Southbound middle valley, constricted corridor and western glacier-fed tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The river continues south through alternately broader multichannel sections and a constricted single-channel mountain corridor. The lower TRIM original overlaps the093C middle map, shows intervening eastern and western tributaries, and follows the selected river to a major western tributary arriving from the glacier/lake complex. The selection stays on the southward receiving river.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact bank or vertex requirement.
correspondence.name_observation: Klinaklini is the bounded representative/receiving river identity. Names of the lateral glacier, lake and western tributary are left null in this evidence set.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad lower river and actual Knight Inlet estuary
correspondence.finding: Below the western tributary junction the mapped river broadens into a braided alluvial corridor, continues south and spreads into the western estuary at the head of Knight Inlet. The primary park map explicitly labels the Klinaklini channels, Knight Inlet, upstream Tsawwati1 and the separate Franklin River mouth east of Dutchman Head. The retained selected terminal falls in this Klinaklini estuarine setting, not in the Franklin River, Homathko River or Bute Inlet.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact bank or vertex requirement.
correspondence.name_observation: Klinaklini River and Knight Inlet are directly mapped terminal names. The representative identity does not establish one scalar hydronym for all upstream selected components.

finding: The headward approach lies east of the Sierra Baguales divide in the valley north of Cerro Ciudadela and Cerro Pináculo. IGN maps a small upper drainage entering the labeled Ensenada de Falcón course, which meets the Flores headwater network and then the labeled Vizcachas receiving course. The exact source spring or individual name of the short initial approach is not established.

The selected route proceeds east/southeast into the Vizcachas corridor, with Arroyo de Bueno approaching from the north. It descends south past the Vizcachas ranch/valley setting, turns west in the Cerro Palique sector and crosses into Chile in the mapped Vizcachas border corridor. Wetland markings accompany parts of the valley; the western Portugués, Dulcinea and Palique lagoons are separate from the selected line.

The westward Vizcachas approach and Baguales/Las Chinas junction area are directly visible. The selected continuation then follows the southward and lower westward Las Chinas corridor, with the Don Guillermo feeder joining from the east.

Lower Las Chinas reaches the eastern shore of Lago del Toro. The rendered route traverses the lake and turns to its western outlet, consistent with the waterbody outline, the DGA river/lake map and the reported Serrano outlet. Its lake crossing is a modeled connecting passage, not a named open river.
correspondence.correspondence: Whole upper, Argentine east–south–west bend, Chilean junction and lake-entry/crossing/outlet fragment inspected against original IGN historical cartography, DGA study cartography, and MMA hydrographic/land-cover views.
correspondence.name_scope: Multiple named river and lake components; no whole-FID scalar hydronym.

finding: The fragment starts at the western Lago del Toro outlet setting and follows the west/southwest Serrano course. The Grey feeder from the northwest joins this corridor; original hydrography separates the tributary from the selected receiving river.

The DGA 2016 map labels the lake outlet and receiving river separately and its prose explicitly identifies Serrano as the lake outlet. MMA linework and the COT waterbody/land outline independently support this geography.
correspondence.correspondence: Whole western lake-outlet and upper Serrano reach inspected.
correspondence.name_scope: Serrano is supported for this river reach, with no scalar application to the selected system.

finding: The selected continuation follows the mapped lower Serrano corridor through the Tyndall/Geikie feeder area and southward valley to the coastal land margin. Original MMA hydrography visibly follows the receiving river to the terminal, while COT shows the coastal indentation reached by that course.

DGA primary prose identifies the terminus as Seno Última Esperanza. The INTA report’s explicitly attributed reproduction of the CFI regional map also shows the Serrano–seno connection, used only as supporting reproduced cartography.
correspondence.correspondence: Whole lower southward Serrano course and actual coastal terminal inspected.
correspondence.name_scope: Serrano receiving reach; no tributary/lake renaming.

correspondence.finding: The head starts on a short north-side feeder, then occupies a short part of the upper Ñirehuao/Coichel corridor before turning northeast toward the eastern upland/boundary band. The original hydrographic map identifies the receiving natural river but does not name the short feeder. The DIRPLAN relief map and COT original establish the surrounding land setting.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: No single hydronym for the entire mixed component; no exact bank or start-point claim.

correspondence.finding: This stored border-aligned component runs through the eastern international-boundary/upland margin near the La Katterfeld sector. DIRPLAN maps that band separately from the natural Ñirehuao/Coichel river west of it; detailed MMA hydrography shows the natural southward channel and La Horqueta tributary. COT shows the adjoining terrestrial setting.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Positive geographic correspondence to the boundary/land band does not support a river name or fluvial connector.

correspondence.finding: The initial southwest return reaches the mapped Ñirehuao/Coichel valley. The ensuing natural river follows its broad southeastern loop, turns northwest and west through the Ñirehuao setting, receives Río Norte and continues to the north-coming Mañihuales/Picaflor corridor. The head and middle original views overlap across this entire route.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Ñirehuao/Coichel applies to the natural river portion, not the initial return across the eastern land/boundary margin.

correspondence.finding: Below the Ñirehuao junction the selected corridor turns southwest, follows the broad Mañihuales valley and receives Cañón and Emperador Guillermo before continuing toward the Simpson junction. Hydrography and DIRPLAN show the route and material side connections; DGA 2004 provides the explicit Mañihuales reach limits.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Aisen labels appear upstream in SIMBIO; this conflicting label extent is not adopted as the DGA-defined name transition.

correspondence.finding: The component continues south from lower Mañihuales, receives the east-coming Simpson, then follows the Aysén westward meanders to the Blanco Oeste confluence. The named junction is explicit in DGA 2004 and corresponds geographically to the original hydrography and DIRPLAN map.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: The component crosses the Mañihuales–Aysén name transition; no uniform component scalar is asserted.

correspondence.finding: Below Blanco Oeste the selected line follows the Aysén channel west through the Puerto Aysén setting, adjoining the northern Pangal/Los Palos-side drainage and reaching the coastal channel/island mouth. Original hydrography, COT coast/water polygons and DIRPLAN regional cartography show the river-to-fjord setting. The municipal Las Ranas description hosted by MMA identifies the receiving southeastern head of Fiordo Aysén.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Rendered sea extension is interpreted at estuarine/fjord corridor scale, without an exact mouth-point or bank assertion.

correspondence.finding: The southern start occupies the Lago Caro northern outlet setting. It continues north in the Blanco valley, with successive bends and tributary settings, to immediately upstream of the Riesco/Quetro receiving area. The original hydrographic map labels Blanco; COT distinguishes Lago Caro and the river corridor from the neighboring lake surfaces; DIRPLAN labels Caro and shows the northward valley.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Starts at the outlet setting; no selected traverse through the wider Caro–Elizalde lake system is inferred.

correspondence.finding: The lower Blanco branch passes the west-entering Río Riesco outlet from Lago Riesco and the east-entering Río Quetro, then runs north/northeast to the Aysén confluence. Original hydrography and COT show all these connector settings; DGA 2004 separately places Blanco west between Lago Caro, the Riesco-outlet station and Aysén.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Riesco is the side-lake/outlet identity; it is not substituted for the complete Blanco Oeste component.

correspondence.finding: Complete source-covered corridor. Clear Río Seco correspondence after the initial unnamed modeled plain bend; lower reach and receiving lagoon context directly observed. The initial naming discrepancy is not classified as missing cartographic coverage.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire FID, including the initial dry/plain bend, intervening valley, eastward lower cañadón, local junctions, lagoon approach and adjacent shoreline, inspected in one complete original IGN map image and local reading crops.
correspondence.name_scope: Reach names only; whole-object candidate and scalar remain null.

observations: The selected western start lies in the dry plateau west of Ea. Inés. It first runs generally south/southeast, turns east across the plain and reaches the cartographically mapped Río Seco approach near the estancia.

The original map shows scattered short broken-blue drainages, small depressions and a stronger drainage system southwest of this bend, but does not establish one named natural river matching the whole modeled initial bend. The plain and connector setting are fully visible; no unseen source interval remains.

subcomponents.part: Upper and middle Río Seco valley
observations: From the Ea. Inés approach, the selected line follows the long northeastward mapped drainage past Ea. Mirasol/Ea. Río Seco, La Josefina and Mulak Aike, then the broad valley through La Margary and La Calandria toward Loma Alta/Don José María.

The original map repeatedly labels the connected valley Río Seco and depicts broken-blue channels, flats and elongated shallow depressions. Coverage includes the full intervening route and tributary entrances, rather than isolated name labels.
The valley receives short side drainages, then turns east below Gran Bajo Bandera Argentina. That separately labelled depression is not silently made the terminal basin of the selected line.

subcomponents.part: Eastern lower cañadón and material junctions
observations: The mapped eastward course passes the Manantiales setting and continues through Ea. Los Toldos toward Ea. Los Cisnes. The lower reach is labelled Cñd. Río Seco.
The Anderson cañadón joins the lower corridor in the Los Toldos sector. The selected path continues east on Río Seco and turns south toward the lagoon; it is not reassigned the Anderson name.

Laguna Tordillo is visibly north of the selected final reach, and Cañadón Porfiado occupies a separate approach south of it. No selected lake transit through Tordillo or reservoir passage is required.

After Los Cisnes the selected line turns south into the northwestern approach of the Laguna Dulce depression. The original image shows the lower Río Seco approach, the labelled lagoon and the adjacent Atlantic shoreline together. The modeled endpoint is not treated as an open-sea mouth.
The original map is historical and generalized. It establishes the terminal basin context but not a currently open, perennial outlet across the coastal margin.

The earlier successfully read prose of Guido and de Barrio (2004), pp.361–362, independently locates Río Seco relative to Laguna Dulce and reports its Atlantic drainage through the lagoon. Its figure was not obtained and contributes no cartographic evidence.
